meta.note: Preview data. All records are Awaiting Evidence Review. Descriptions were drawn from publisher and repository pages retrieved on this date and are not a substitute for the full papers.

similarities.text: Both make predictions about neural correlates of visual consciousness that were stated in advance for a joint test.
Both are among the four approaches reviewed in a 2022 survey of theories of consciousness.

contrasts.a: A fronto-parietal network alongside high-level sensory cortex.
contrasts.test: Compare conscious versus nonconscious trials across brain regions with fMRI, M-EEG, and intracranial EEG.

contrasts.a: Content should be decodable in prefrontal-parietal areas and high-level sensory cortex.
contrasts.b: Content should be most decodable from posterior cortex.
contrasts.test: Decode stimulus category or content from activity in each region during conscious perception.

contrasts.a: A brief ignition at onset; the workspace need not stay active throughout a durable conscious experience.
contrasts.b: The substrate persists across the whole experience.
contrasts.test: Track activity over the duration of a stimulus, including at offset.

contrasts.a: Higher prefrontal and parietal activity before a stimulus lowers the chance it is perceived.
contrasts.b: Greater excitability or synchrony in posterior and early visual areas raises the chance of perception.
contrasts.test: Relate pre-stimulus activity to whether the stimulus is later reported.

contrasts.a: Long-range synchronization between prefrontal nodes and category-selective areas.
contrasts.b: Synchronization between category-selective areas and early visual areas.
contrasts.test: Measure synchronization between these region pairs during conscious perception.

reported.text: A 2025 report of this test described results that partly align with predictions of both theories while substantially challenging key claims of each, including no sustained posterior synchronization and a general lack of ignition at stimulus offset. The authors do not present either theory as proven or disproven.

items.note: The contrasts are those stated by the proponents for this specific test.

similarities.text: Both are named in one formal critique as theories that tie consciousness to causal structure.

items.note: Specific contrasting predictions: Awaiting Evidence Review.

contrasts.a: Integration alone does not produce awareness; an attention model must also be computed and bound to content, according to the authors' comparison.
contrasts.b: Not specified in the sources read for this comparison.

items.note: One side of this contrast is the AST authors' own framing of global workspace and integration theories, not a statement from GNWT proponents.
